A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same work, A Generic Framework for Conformal Fairness. All 33 pages of each version, including Appendices A–E, are readable and support comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix E report original experiments measuring fairness disparities and prediction-set efficiency on five graph and tabular datasets, including comparisons with baseline conformal predictors and BatchGCP.

after.justification: The later version retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and Appendix E, including the classwise-threshold, intersectional-fairness, and BatchGCP comparisons.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, threshold selection, classwise thresholds, fairness-metric extensions, and the auditing procedure are unchanged. The APS citation correction does not alter its scoring function or implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ACSIncome, ACSEducation, Credit, Pokec-n, and Pokec-z with the same classification tasks and sensitive-attribute scenarios. Single-attribute and intersectional evaluations are retained.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain the same baseline conformal predictors using APS, RAPS, TPS, CFGNN, and DAPS. Appendix E.6 retains the same Base APS, BatchGCP, and CF comparisons.

E3.justification: The 30%/20%/25%/25% data split, baseline coverage target of 0.9, fairness thresholds, evaluation metrics, model choices, and hyperparameter search spaces remain unchanged. No evaluation procedure is added or revised.

E4.justification: Appendix E retains the same shared-versus-classwise threshold analyses, sensitive-attribute comparisons, intersectional analyses, and BatchGCP group-coverage diagnostic. Caption corrections do not introduce new analyses.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including averaging baseline performance across thresholds. Neither version supplies experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests that differ from the other.

E6.justification: All reported numerical entries and plotted outcomes are retained. For example, Table E6 reports ACSEducation disparate impact of 0.011 for Base APS, 0.576 for BatchGCP, and 0.781 for CF in both versions. Caption edits correct panel references without changing findings.

T1.justification: The fairness definitions, Lemmas 3.1–3.3, Theorem 3.4, Corollary C.1, and proofs and derivations in Appendices B–C are unchanged. Equation-spacing differences do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about a flexible conformal-fairness framework, exchangeability-based applicability to graph data, fairness control, and auditing.

C2.justification: The fairness–efficiency tradeoff, intersectional calibration-data limitations, predictive-parity conditions, and interpretation of BatchGCP undercoverage remain unchanged. Revised directional references in captions preserve the existing explanations.

D1.justification: Appendix D.3 removes the statement that source code is provided in supplementary material. The repository link in the reproducibility statement remains, as do the implementation details, hyperparameter tables, and P100 hardware disclosure. This changes access documentation without establishing that code availability changed.

R1.justification: Appendix D.2 changes the APS attribution from Romano et al. (2019), listed as Conformalized quantile regression, to Romano et al. (2020), listed as Classification with valid and adaptive coverage. Both works were already referenced; this is a limited attribution correction, with broader research positioning unchanged.

P1.justification: The revision makes localized punctuation and wording edits in the dataset descriptions, Appendix E introduction, and figure captions. The narrative, section sequence, and substantive explanations remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1's caption changes left/right to top/bottom; Figures 2–3 drop incorrect panel counts; Figures E2 and E6–E9 correct directional references. Local reflow moves the E.1 heading onto page 19 and shifts tables and Figure E1 upward. The plotted content and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Correcting misleading panel directions and counts makes several figures easier to interpret, and the APS citation now agrees with Section 3.6 and the listed classification paper. Removing the supplementary-code statement does not eliminate the retained repository pointer. These are limited improvements in clarity and attribution; the scientific methods, evidence, and conclusions remain unchanged.
